57214875051; 58194321400; 57206601150; 58846815700; 57215196148; 41862317600; 56043579700; 58915780800; 7202851756
Intra-hour solar irradiance forecasting using topology data analysis and physics-driven deep learning
(2024) Renewable Energy, 224, art. no. 120138, Cited 7 times.
DOI: 10.1016/j.renene.2024.120138
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85186490805?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Systems Engineering Institute, School of Automation, Xi'an Jiaotong University, Shaanxi, Xi'an, 710049, China; School of Future Technology, Xi'an Jiaotong University, Shaanxi, Xi'an, 710049, China; Qinghai Photovoltaic Industry Innovation Centre Co.Ltd, State Power Investment Corporation, Qinghai, Xining, 810000, China; Northwest Engineering Corporation Limited, POWERCHINA, Shaanxi, Xi'an, 710065, China
ABSTRACT: Real-time Direct Normal Irradiance (DNI) prediction is crucial for reliable and economic operation of Concentrated photothermal Solar Power (CSP) system in arid desert areas. However, the stochastic characteristics of short-term multidimensional meteorological time series make intra-hour DNI prediction a challenging task. In this study, we have proposed a deep learning model called TLD, which is combined with topological features captured by Topology Data Analysis (TDA) and temporal features captured by LSTM to address this challenge. Experimental results demonstrated that TLD outperformed the five latest models (Ridge, RF, C_GRU, BiLSTM, and GBRT) on seven solar radiation datasets in arid desert areas. Further analysis revealed that the proportion of cloudy days is a key factor affecting the model's performance. To enhance the forecast ability of TLD, we developed a physics-informed hybrid model named TLDP based on TLD and a smart persistence model, which fully combines the DNI prediction ability of TLD under cloudy conditions and that of the smart persistence model under sunny conditions. Experimental results of eight datasets collected from real-world solar photothermal power stations indicated that TLDP outperformed existing models, which may lay a foundation for more economical and stable operation of CSP plants in arid desert areas. © 2024 Elsevier Ltd

Assessment of hybrid bidirectional deep learning models for short-term global horizontal irradiance forecasting
(2024) AIP Conference Proceedings, 3214 (1), art. no. 020034, Cited 4 times.
DOI: 10.1063/5.0239497
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85210423164?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Laboratory of Signals & Systems, Institute of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, University m'Hamed Bougara, Boumerdes, 35000, Algeria; Department of Electrical Engineering, Graphic Era (Deemed to Be University), Dehradun, 248002, India; Electronics Department, SET Laboratory Organization, Faculty of Technology, Blida 1 University, Blida, Algeria; Laboratoire de Technologie Industrielle et de l'Information, Faculté de Technologie, Université de Bejaia, Bejaia, 06000, Algeria; Graphic Era Hill University, Dehradun, 248002, India; Applied Science Research Center, Applied Science Private University, Amman, 11937, Jordan
ABSTRACT: Incorporating renewable energy sources, particularly solar electricity, into power grids is crucial for environmental sustainability. However, the intermittent nature of solar irradiation creates operational and control issues. To address this, anticipating global horizontal irradiance (GHI) is critical. This study describes a novel hybrid deep learning-based forecasting system called the Convolutional Neural Network and Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory (CNN-BiLSTM) model. In terms of accuracy and performance, this model is compared to three other hybrid models: The Convolutional Neural Network Long Short Term Memory (CNN-LSTM), the Convolutional Neural Network Gated Recurrent Unit (CNN-GRU), and the Convolutional Neural Network Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (CNN-BiGRU). The comparison focuses on yearly predicting Global Horizontal Irradiance (GHI) with a 1-hour timeframe in Alice Springs, Australia. The models' accuracy is evaluated using four metrics: root mean squared error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), coefficient of determination (R^2), and normalized root mean square (nRMSE). The results show that the suggested model outperforms the other models. © 2024 Author(s).

Advanced simulation-based predictive modelling for solar irradiance sensor farms
(2025) Journal of Simulation, 19 (3), pp. 265 - 282, Cited 3 times.
DOI: 10.1080/17477778.2024.2333775
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85189614671?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Department of Computer Architecture and Automation, Universidad Complutense de Madrid, Madrid, Spain; Department of Computer Systems Architecture and Technology, Universidad Politécnica de Madrid, Madrid, Spain
ABSTRACT: The need for accurate solar power forecasting is critical for grid stability as solar energy becomes more prevalent. This paper presents a new framework called Cloud-based Analysis and Integration for Data Efficiency (CAIDE) for real-time monitoring and forecasting of solar irradiance in sensor farms. CAIDE can handle multiple sensor farms, enhance predictive models in real-time, and is built on Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies. It can correct its forecasts, ensuring they stay current, and operates on various architectures, ensuring scalability. Tested on multiple sensor farms, CAIDE proved to be scalable and improved the initial accuracy of solar power production forecasts in real-time. This framework is significant for solar plant deployment and the advancement of renewable energy. © 2024 The Operational Research Society.

Generalized global solar radiation forecasting model via cyber-secure deep federated learning
(2024) Environmental Science and Pollution Research, 31 (12), pp. 18281 - 18295, Cited 10 times.
DOI: 10.1007/s11356-023-30224-1
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85174171483?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Faculty of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Tabriz, Tabriz, 5166616471, Iran; GECAD - Research Group on Intelligent Engineering and Computing for Advanced Innovation and Development, LASI - Intelligent Systems Associate Laboratory, Polytechnic of Porto, Porto, P-4200-072, Portugal; School of Energy Systems, LUT University, Lappeenranta, Finland; SYSTEC-ARISE Research Center for Systems and Technologies, Electrical and Computer Enginnering Department, Faculty of Engineering, University of Porto, Porto, P-4200 465, Portugal; Department of Energy (AAU Energy), Aalborg University, Aalborg, 9220, Denmark; Institute of High Voltage & High Current, Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Universiti Teknologi Malaysia, Johor Bahru, Malaysia
ABSTRACT: Recently, the increasing prevalence of solar energy in power and energy systems around the world has dramatically increased the importance of accurately predicting solar irradiance. However, the lack of access to data in many regions and the privacy concerns that can arise when collecting and transmitting data from distributed points to a central server pose challenges to current predictive techniques. This study proposes a global solar radiation forecasting approach based on federated learning (FL) and convolutional neural network (CNN). In addition to maintaining input data privacy, the proposed procedure can also be used as a global supermodel. In this paper, data related to eight regions of Iran with different climatic features are considered as CNN input for network training in each client. To test the effectiveness of the global supermodel, data related to three new regions of Iran named Abadeh, Jarqavieh, and Arak are used. It can be seen that the global forecasting supermodel was able to forecast solar radiation for Abadeh, Jarqavieh, and Arak regions with 95%, 92%, and 90% accuracy coefficients, respectively. Finally, in a comparative scenario, various conventional machine learning and deep learning models are employed to forecast solar radiation in each of the study regions. The results of the above approaches are compared and evaluated with the results of the proposed FL-based method. The results show that, since no training data were available from regions of Abadeh, Jarqavieh, and Arak, the conventional methods were not able to forecast solar radiation in these regions. This evaluation confirms the high ability of the presented FL approach to make acceptable predictions while preserving privacy and eliminating model reliance on training data. © The Author(s) 2023.

Review of Data-Driven Approaches Applied to Time-Series Solar Irradiance Forecasting for Future Energy Networks
(2025) Energies, 18 (21), art. no. 5823, Cited 2 times.
DOI: 10.3390/en18215823
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105021458736?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: School of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Sydney, Sydney, 2006, NSW, Australia
ABSTRACT: The fast-increasing penetration of photovoltaic (PV) power raises the issue of grid stability due to its intermittency and lack of inertia in power systems. Solar irradiance forecasting effectively supports advanced control, mitigates power intermittency, and improves grid resilience. Irradiance forecasting based on data-driven methods aims to predict the direction and level of power variation and indicate quick action. This article presents a comprehensive review and comparative analysis of data-driven approaches for time-series solar irradiance forecasting. It systematically evaluates nineteen representative models spanning from traditional statistical methods to state-of-the-art deep learning architectures across multiple performance dimensions that are critical for practical deployment. The analysis aims to provide actionable insights for researchers and practitioners when selecting and implementing suitable forecasting solutions for diverse solar energy applications. © 2025 by the authors.

Prototype-based Implementation of AI for Enhanced Solar Photovoltaic Performance
(2026) Proceedings of the 2026 International Conference on AI-Driven Smart Systems and Ubiquitous Computing, ICAUC 2026, pp. 277 - 283, Cited 1 times.
DOI: 10.1109/ICAUC68182.2026.11441260
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105037428756?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Rgm College of Engineering & Technology, Dept. of Cse (AI & ML), Nandyal, India; Bapatla Engineering College, Dept. of Information Technology, Bapatla, India; Nbkr Institute of Science & Technology, Dept. of Cse, Kota, India
ABSTRACT: This paper presents the design and implementation of a prototype based solar photovoltaic (PV) system enhanced by, the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) methods. The intention of the work described was to increase the reliability of solar power forecasting and to provide an automated fault detection system in PV installations. The authors created an experimental apparatus using a microcontroller-based data acquisition system, environmental sensors and a solar panel. The experimental apparatus collected RT data including solar irradiance, temperature, humidity, voltage and current over 30 days. The authors then trained a predictive power output machine-learning model using a Random Forest Regressor and their collected dataset. The Random forest Regressor model produced a prediction accuracy of 91%, indicating this model is reliable for estimating solar energy production given the changeability in climate condition. In addition, the authors implemented a fault detection module using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) that analyzed the panel images for problems like dust and physical damage. Their CNN reached 94.7% precision demonstrating its ability to classify faults in real time. The prototype system was preconfigured with wireless communication technology to allow for remote monitoring via mobile dashboard. The experimental findings validated the point of plausible AI integrated PV systems can be used to optimize energy efficiency, enable prognostic maintenance, and decrease operational losses. All in all, this is a contribution to the emerging field of intelligent, cost-effective and scalable solar energy management applications that can be deployed in decentralized and rural areas.  © 2026 IEEE.

Physics-informed deep operator network for real-time dynamic simulation of extruded-absorber photovoltaic/thermal collectors
(2026) Applied Thermal Engineering, 289, art. no. 129695, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1016/j.applthermaleng.2026.129695
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105027940153?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Department of Mechanical Engineering, Babol Noshirvani University of Technology, P.O. Box 484, Babol, Iran; Department of Mechanical Engineering, North Tehran Branch, Islamic Azad University, Tehran, Iran
ABSTRACT: Photovoltaic/thermal (PVT) collectors with extruded absorbers offer superior thermal coupling and enhanced heat extraction compared to conventional sheet-and-tube designs. However, their dynamic modeling under realistic, time-varying environmental and operational conditions remains computationally prohibitive for real-time applications such as digital twins, predictive control, and online optimization. To address this gap, this study introduces a novel hybrid physics-informed deep operator network (PINN-DeepONet) specifically tailored for PVT-water collectors. A high-fidelity transient numerical model based on first-principles energy balances was developed and solved across variable solar irradiance (43–850 W/m²), ambient temperatures (22–25 °C), wind speeds (1–4 m/s), and coolant mass flow rates (2.8–14.1 kg/h) to generate a comprehensive training dataset. The proposed PINN-DeepONet uniquely integrates operator learning with embedded thermodynamic constraints, ensuring physical consistency while enabling ultra-fast inference. The model accurately predicts the spatiotemporal temperature evolution across all seven structural layers of the PVT collector, achieving a mean absolute error (MAE) below 0.8 °C and a coefficient of determination (R²) exceeding 0.99. Rigorous validation against both experimental and numerical benchmarks confirms the framework’s reliability. By enabling millisecond-level dynamic simulation without sacrificing physical fidelity, this approach provides a robust foundation for real-time digital twin deployment, control, and optimal design of advanced water-cooled extruded-absorber PVT systems. The methodology is readily extensible to other hybrid energy systems governed by coupled thermal–electrical dynamics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Kaysal K., Hocaoglu F.O., Öztürk N.
AUTHOR FULL NAMES: Kaysal, Kübra (56038589500); Hocaoglu, Fatih Onur (23473495100); Öztürk, Nihat (23968464700)

Short-term forecasting of solar irradiance and temperature using deep learning models with multiple inputs and multiple outputs [Çok girdili-çok değişkenli çıktıya sahip derin öğrenme modelleri ile kısa vadeli güneş ışınım şiddeti ve sıcaklık tahmini]
(2026) Journal of the Faculty of Engineering and Architecture of Gazi University, 41 (1), pp. 463 - 478, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.17341/gazimmfd.1533969
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105034708260?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Department of Electrical and Energy, Afyon Vocational School, Afyon Kocatepe University, Afyonkarahisar, 03200, Turkey; Department of Electrical Engineering, Engineering of Faculty, Afyon Kocatepe University, Afyonkarahisar, 03200, Turkey; Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Faculty of Technology, Gazi University, Ankara, 06560, Turkey
ABSTRACT: The intermittent and fluctuating nature of solar radiation poses significant limitations for many applications. Accurate estimation of solar radiation is a crucial factor in predicting the output power of a photovoltaic system. In this study, the effects of multivariate inputs on bivariate outputs for short-term forecasts were examined, and the impact of meteorological changes on a solar power plant planned for a specific region was investigated. Additionally, the performance of various deep learning models and their hybrid combinations for predicting solar radiation and temperature was compared. Compared to other models, the M/CNN-BILSTM_II model demonstrated the best performance in estimating both temperature and radiation intensity using the three input parameters: temperature, solar radiation, and humidity. The performance of the models was evaluated using RMSE, MAE, NRMSE, SMAPE, and R² metrics. For solar radiation, these metrics were calculated as 71,21 W/m² (RMSE), 35,42 W/m² (MAE), %6,52 (NRMSE), %14,87 (SMAPE) and %94,78 (R²), respectively. For temperature values, RMSE was obtained as RMSE 0,76°C, MAE 0,54°C, NRMSE %1,59, SMAPE %12,14 and R² %99,23. © 2026, Gazi Universitesi. All rights reserved.

Shan S., Dou W., Sreeram V., Li C., Wang K., Zhang K., Wei H.
AUTHOR FULL NAMES: Shan, Shuo (57215671898); Dou, Weijing (57219803767); Sreeram, Victor (7005065836); Li, Chenxi (36809881600); Wang, Kai (58367020200); Zhang, Kanjian (7404451787); Wei, Haikun (7402516860)
57215671898; 57219803767; 7005065836; 36809881600; 58367020200; 7404451787; 7402516860
SolarFM: Spatio-temporal solar irradiance forecasting based on time series foundation model
(2026) Applied Energy, 410, art. no. 127532, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1016/j.apenergy.2026.127532
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105030025894?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Key Laboratory of Measurement and Control of Complex Systems of Engineering, Ministry of Education, School of Automation, Southeast University, Nanjing, 210096, China; Southeast University Shenzhen Research Institute, Shenzhen, 518063, China; Department of Electrical, Electronics and Computer Engineering, The University of Western Australia, Perth, Australia; State Key Laboratory of Technology and Equipment for Defense against Power System Operational Risks, Nanjing, 211106, China; NARI Technology Co., Ltd., Nanjing, 211106, China
ABSTRACT: Accurate solar irradiance prediction plays a pivotal role in optimizing photovoltaic system operations and enhancing grid integration efficiency. Existing deep learning methods use diverse encoder architectures for spatiotemporal irradiance forecasting. However, they often fail to effectively decouple cross-channel temporal dependencies, limiting their capacity to capture complex irradiance variation patterns. To overcome this challenge, SolarFM, is introduced as an innovative spatiotemporal forecasting framework inspired by time series foundation models. The proposed method begins with zero-shot forecasting using localized meteorological sequences. It capitalizes on foundation models’ generalization ability, gained through pretraining on vast temporal data, to correlate irradiance patterns with weather variables. A dual-branch spatiotemporal encoder is subsequently designed to synergistically process historical observations and forecasted sequences, where a tensor factorization network extracts high-dimensional temporal representations from future sequence projections. The framework ultimately integrates multimodal features through adaptive fusion to generate synchronized multi-region irradiance predictions. Comprehensive evaluations on public datasets demonstrate that SolarFM achieves 2.6%–15.1% accuracy improvements in single-step and multi-step forecasting tasks compared to baseline methods. Furthermore, systematic experiments reveal remarkable robustness under diverse meteorological conditions and superior performance consistency in high-irradiance scenarios, establishing its potential as a paradigm-shifting solution for solar energy forecasting systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

A Stochastic Predictive Control Framework for Photovoltaic Maximization using Coupled LSTM-DQN Architectures in Volatile Climatic Environments
(2026) ICCES 2026 - Conference Proceedings of 2026 the 2nd International Conference Computing and Emerging Sciences, pp. 78 - 85, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1145/3797491.3797518
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105038051280?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Altinbas University, İstanbul, Turkey
ABSTRACT: Traditional solar trackers often lose energy and experience mechanical problems in cloudy weather because they react rigidly to changing conditions. Studies evaluated the Hybrid LSTM-DQN control on testing dataset of 120 hours of high-resolution (1-minute) weather data to provide a fair assessment. This paper suggests a new control system to fix these problems. It combines a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, which predicts how much sunlight there will be soon, with a Deep Q-Network (DQN) reinforcement learning agent, which makes the best decisions. The LSTM predicts sunlight intensity for the coming 10 minutes with a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 42.8 W/m2. This prediction helps the DQN controller. When tested using 120 hours of weather data, the new system had a Net Energy Gain of 17.8% (28.4 kWh) compared to a regular PID tracker. The system also stopped unnecessary movements, cutting down actuator uses by 34.8% and lowering daily motor power use to 108 Wh. These results show that using predictive deep learning along with stochastic control can greatly improve how well photovoltaic tracking systems work and how long they last. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s)

Solar Irradiance Forecasting With Deep Learning and Ensemble Models: LSTM, Random Forest and Extra Trees With Multivariate Meteorological Data
(2025) IET Smart Grid, 8 (1), art. no. e70019, Cited 8 times.
DOI: 10.1049/stg2.70019
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105010564773?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Facultad de Ingeniería y Ciencias Aplicadas, Universidad de las Américas, Quito, Ecuador; Escola Superior de Tecnologia e Gestão, Polytechnic Institute of Leiria, Leiria, Portugal; V-Kallpa, Toulouse, France; Energy Transition Research Group, Universidad Politécnica Salesiana, Cuenca, Ecuador
ABSTRACT: The penetration of solar energy within power systems is imperative to ensure the enduring sustainability of power systems, especially in cases of isolated systems such as microgrids. However, the variability in solar energy generation, which can impact grid stability and supply-demand balance, highlights the necessity for reliable forecasting methods and advanced technological tools in addressing power system challenges. This paper presents an in-depth exploration of solar irradiance forecasting, utilising a combination of advanced techniques, including deep learning and ensemble models. In particular, the utilisation of long short-term memory (LSTM), random forest and extra trees in conjunction with multivariate meteorological data is investigated to enhance the accuracy and reliability of solar irradiance predictions. A comprehensive technique for modelling multivariate time series is employed to predict solar irradiance by incorporating various meteorological factors, such as temperature, relative humidity, and barometric pressure, among other relevant variables. A case study in Cuenca, Ecuador, was chosen based on real data obtained from a meteorological station, ensuring the accuracy and reliability of the data. The proposed method significantly enhances performance when compared to a baseline model, with the LSTM model notably excelling in predicting maximum and minimum solar irradiance, offering valuable insights for extended forecasting applications. © 2025 The Author(s). Spatial and temporal super-resolution methods for high-fidelity solar imaging
(2025) Astronomy and Astrophysics, 695, art. no. A105, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1051/0004-6361/202452638
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/86000625059?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv, Glushkova Ave., 4, Kyiv, 03127, Ukraine; Department of Physics, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong; Center for Computation Astrophysics, Flatiron Institute, New York, 10010, NY, United States; Department of Astrophysical Sciences, Princeton University, 4 Ivy Lane, Princeton, 08544, NJ, United States; Department of Physics & Center for Data Science, New York University, 726 Broadway, New York, 10003, NY, United States
ABSTRACT: Context. The Sun plays a significant role in space weather by emitting energy and electromagnetic radiation that influence the environment around the Earth. Missions such as SOHO, STEREO, and SDO captured solar observations at multiple wavelengths to monitor and predict solar events. However, the data transmission from these missions is often constrained, in particular, for those operating at greater distances from Earth. This limits the availability of continuous observations. Aims. We increase the spatial and temporal resolution of solar images to improve the quality and availability of solar data. By addressing telemetry constraints and providing more detailed solar image reconstructions, we seek to facilitate a more accurate analysis of solar dynamics and improve space weather prediction. Methods. We applied deep-learning techniques, specifically, a UNet-based architecture, to generate high-resolution solar images that enhance the intricate details of the solar structures. Additionally, we used a similar architecture to reconstruct solar image sequences with a reduced temporal resolution to predict missing frames and restore temporal continuity. Results. Our deep-learning approach successfully enhances the resolution of solar images and reveals finer details of solar structures. The model also predicts missing frames in solar image sequences, which allows more continuous observation despite telemetry constraints. These advancements contribute to a better analysis of solar dynamics and set the stage for an improved space weather forecasting and future solar physics research.  © The Authors 2025.

Sharma G., Gupta R.

Accurate global horizontal irradiance estimation with hybrid convolutional neural network-informer-gated recurrent unit framework
(2026) Indian Journal of Physics, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1007/s12648-026-03995-9
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105033288310?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Department of Electrical Engineering, GLA University, UP, Mathura, 281406, India; Department of Computer Science and Engineering, SRM Institute of Science and Technology, Delhi NCR Campus, UP, Ghaziabad, 201204, India
ABSTRACT: Accurate prediction of Global Horizontal Irradiance (GHI) is pivotal for optimizing solar energy generation, improving grid stability, and advancing climate forecasting. This study introduces an innovative hybrid deep learning framework, CNN-Informer-GRU, designed to enhance the precision and robustness of GHI forecasting. The model integrates the strengths of three advanced architectures such as CNN for extracting local features and detecting short-term fluctuations, the Informer model for capturing long-range temporal dependencies through efficient sparse attention mechanisms, and GRU for refining temporal dynamics to boost future predictions. To further elevate performance, a clustering technique such as DBSCAN is employed to group similar GHI patterns based on historical meteorological data. This multi-seasonal clustering spanning summer, rainy, and winter enables the model to focus on season-specific trends, thereby improving accuracy and generalization. The z-score normalization ensures data consistency and smooth convergence during training. The model's effectiveness is rigorously validated on real-world GHI datasets using statistical metrics such as MAE (3.111), MSE (26.8891), RMSE (5.1855), and NRMSE (0.0162), showcasing its superiority over traditional forecasting methods. This work highlights the critical role of hybrid deep learning and data-driven strategies in enabling reliable solar radiation forecasting an essential step toward sustainable energy systems and smarter energy infrastructure. © Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science 2026.

Physics-Guided Spatiotemporal Transformer (Psttransformer) for Short-Term Solar Irradiance Forecasting
(2025) 2025 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia, ISGT Asia 2025, pp. 35 - 41, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1109/ISGTAsia63446.2025.11431555
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105036378370?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: College of Electrical Engineering, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China
ABSTRACT: Accurate solar irradiance forecasting is critical for reliable renewable energy integration, yet traditional machine learning models struggle to capture temporal dynamics and purely data-driven deep learning approaches often lack physical consistency. This study proposes the Physics-Guided Spatiotemporal Transformer (PST-Transformer), which incorporates solar geometry and cloud cover as physicsinformed features to guide model learning. Comparative evaluation against both machine learning and deep learning benchmarks demonstrates that physics-guided hybridization substantially improves forecasting accuracy: CNN-LSTM achieved a 52.6% reduction in MAE, while Transformer-LSTM gained an additional 7.3% improvement when physics-based inputs were included. The proposed PST-Transformer achieved state-of-the-art performance (MAE = 0.0216, RMSE = 0.04199, R2 = 0.9571). These findings highlight that combining physical constraints with deep learning not only enhances robustness under variable weather conditions but also provides a practical pathway for stable large-scale solar integration. © 2025 IEEE.

Umar S., EL-Fouly T.H.M., Al-Durra A.
AUTHOR FULL NAMES: Umar, Shayan (58169923300); EL-Fouly, Tarek H.M (6603219963); Al-Durra, Ahmed (24331074800)
58169923300; 6603219963; 24331074800
Multi-horizon daily solar irradiance forecasting with clear-sky cross attention and decorrelated bagging
(2026) Energy Conversion and Management: X, 30, art. no. 101861, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1016/j.ecmx.2026.101861
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105037788852?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Advanced Power and Energy Center (APEC), Electrical Engineering Department, Khalifa University, Abu Dhabi, 127788, United Arab Emirates
ABSTRACT: Accurate medium-range solar irradiance forecasting remains a computational challenge for existing machine learning models. This study proposes CSI-DECOB-Ensemble, a lightweight modular machine learning model for optimizing grid operations and energy dispatch management. Unlike monolithic multi-vector models, the proposed model decomposes the forecasting task into fifteen submodels, each optimized for a specific daily horizon using Gaussian-weighted lag embeddings. A Clear-Sky Cross-Attention mechanism couples historical atmospheric dynamics with future clear-sky potentials to extract physically consistent features, which are processed via a decorrelated bagging strategy to minimize variance. The proposed model was evaluated across four geographically distinct regions: Abu Dhabi, Aswan, Islamabad, and Longreach. The experimental results show that the proposed model outperforms conventional gradient boosting and deep learning models. In the high-irradiance region of Abu Dhabi, the proposed model achieved an R2 exceeding 0.98 across all horizons. In Islamabad, characterized by high variation in solar irradiation, it reduced the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by up to 26.2% compared to PatchTST at the 5-day horizon, while maintaining lower computational power consumption. The accuracy of the model remained consistent, with low error metrics persisting up to the 15-day horizon, as confirmed by the Friedman test. These findings demonstrate that the CSI-DECOB-Ensemble model is well-suited for applications where computationally efficient frameworks with high accuracy are required for medium-range energy management. © 2026

Cost-effective design of a hybrid renewable energy system based on accurate global horizontal irradiance prediction
(2026) Electric Power Systems Research, 259, art. no. 113224, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1016/j.epsr.2026.113224
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105037437107?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Guangzhou College of Technology and Business, Guangdong province, Guangzhou, 510800, China; Hainan Academy of Forestry, Hainan, Haikou, 571100, China
ABSTRACT: The advancement of renewable energy is a key priority for mitigating climate change, enhancing energy security, and supporting sustainable economic growth. Grid-connected photovoltaic systems play a crucial role in the energy transition; however, their power output is highly dependent on meteorological conditions, making accurate solar irradiance forecasting essential. This study proposes a hybrid deep learning framework that integrates a Series-Aware Graph-Enhanced Transformer (SageFormer) model with a Snow Ablation Optimizer (SAO) to predict Global Horizontal Irradiance (GHI). Comparative analyses demonstrate that the proposed SAO-SageFormer model outperforms benchmark methods, achieving a high prediction accuracy with a coefficient of determination of 0.992 and a root mean square error of 27.31 W/m². The forecasted GHI data are subsequently used to optimize and size a grid-connected renewable energy system in Hami, Xinjiang, China. The optimized system, consisting of photovoltaic panels, battery storage, and a power converter, achieves a net present cost of $100,672,300 and a levelized cost of electricity of 0.098 $/kWh. The results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed approach in designing cost-efficient, reliable, and environmentally sustainable grid-connected renewable energy systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Jacques Molu R.J., Tripathi B., Mbasso W.F., Dzonde Naoussi S.R., Bajaj M., Wira P., Blazek V., Prokop L., Misak S.

Advancing short-term solar irradiance forecasting accuracy through a hybrid deep learning approach with Bayesian optimization
(2024) Results in Engineering, 23, art. no. 102461, Cited 73 times.
DOI: 10.1016/j.rineng.2024.102461
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85196787654?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Technology and Applied Sciences Laboratory, University of Douala, Douala, Cameroon; School of Humanities and Social Sciences, Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology, Patiala, India; Department of Electrical Engineering, Graphic Era (Deemed to be University), Dehradun, 248002, India; Hourani Center for Applied Scientific Research, Al-Ahliyya Amman University, Amman, Jordan; Graphic Era Hill University, Dehradun, 248002, India; Laboratoire IRIMAS, University de Haute Alsace, 61 Rue Albert Camus, Mulhouse, 68200, France; ENET Centre, VSB—Technical University of Ostrava, Ostrava, 708 00, Czech Republic
ABSTRACT: The optimization of solar energy integration into the power grid relies heavily on accurate forecasting of solar irradiance. In this study, a new approach for short-term solar irradiance forecasting is introduced. This method combines Bayesian Optimized Attention-Dilated Long Short-Term Memory and Savitzky-Golay filtering. The methodology is implemented to analyze data obtained from a solar irradiance probe situated in Douala, Cameroon. Initially, the unprocessed data is augmented by integrating distinctive solar irradiation variables, and the Savitzky-Golay filter with Bayesian Optimization is used to enhance its quality. Subsequently, multiple deep learning models, including Long Short-Term Memory, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory, Artificial Neural Networks, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory with Additive Attention Mechanism, and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory with Additive Attention Mechanism and Dilated Convolutional layers, are trained and evaluated. Out of all the models considered, the proposed approach, which combines the attention mechanism and dilated convolutional layers, demonstrates exceptional performance with the best convergence and accuracy in forecasting. Bayesian Optimization is further utilized to fine-tune the polynomial and window size of the Savitzky-Golay filter and optimize the hyperparameters of the deep learning models. The results show a Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error of 0.6564, a Normalized Root Mean Square Error of 0.2250, and a Root Mean Square Error of 22.9445, surpassing previous studies in the literature. Empirical findings highlight the effectiveness of the proposed methodology in enhancing the accuracy of short-term solar irradiance forecasting. This research contributes to the field by introducing novel data pre-processing techniques, a hybrid deep learning architecture, and the development of a benchmark dataset. These advancements benefit both researchers and solar plant managers, improving solar irradiance forecasting capabilities. © 2024 The Author(s)

Artificial Intelligence Models for Short Term PV Forecasting for Direct PV to EV System
(2025) 2025 IEEE Power Electronics Society International Decentralized Energy Access Symposium, IDEAS 2025, Cited 1 times.
DOI: 10.1109/IDEAS62193.2025.11157383
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105019059888?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: PT PLN Engineering, Engineering Department, Jakarta, Indonesia; PT PLN Indonesia Power, Generation Business Development, Jakarta, Indonesia
ABSTRACT: The fast expansion of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems and the widespread adoption of electric vehicles (EV) in the future may lead to a mismatch between supply and demand, posing challenges for distribution operators. One potential solution to this issue is the direct integration of PV to EV, reducing the reliance on Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). However, a key challenge with solar PV technology is its dependence on intermittent factors such as cloud cover and weather conditions. To tackle this, Artificial Intelligence (AI) models and datasets can be used for short-term PV energy output forecasting. This paper presents an extensive review of recent research (2014-2024) in short-term solar energy forecasting and the case of direct PV to EV charging. The review analyzes content from reputable academic sources, assessing the performance of deep learning models, the availability of open-source datasets, and their implications for direct EV charging. Notably, M-CNN-L and GRU algorithms demonstrate superior accuracy in short-term solar energy forecasting. The integration of ground-based cloud images with time-series weather data greatly improves predictive accuracy. Direct PV to EV system is not yet widely implemented, due to challenge in DC protection system and complex infrastructure planning. Moreover, valuable online datasets, including meteorological data, historical solar irradiance, and cloud images, are available for research and practical use. Nevertheless, gaps exist in model performance and evaluation metrics. This paper provides recommendations for future research, such as refining methodologies, improving datasets, and developing customized evaluation metrics tailored to network management and future electricity with flexible market pricing. These suggestions aim to advance the field of short-term PV forecasting for direct PV to EV system development.  © 2025 IEEE.

A Hybrid Approach for Time Series Solar Irradiance Forecasting
(2025) Colloquium in Information Science and Technology, CIST, pp. 286 - 291, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1109/CiSt65886.2025.11224232
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105024942334?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Ibnou Zohr University, Laboratory Peti, Ouarzazate, Morocco
ABSTRACT: Forecasting solar irradiance is of great interest in renewable energy production, as it enables the anticipation of energy output and helps maintain a stable balance between generation and demand. However, it still presents a challenging task due to the complex nature of solar irradiance time series under variable and unpredictable weather conditions. The aim of this paper is to forecast solar irradiance by merging Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models for feature extraction, followed by Random Forest Regression to predict future values. The approach is used to predict short-term solar irradiance using a real world dataset from two different geographical sites and under four different weather conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach improves forecasting performance over simple deep learning models using the same dataset. The effectiveness of the hybrid model is also discussed through comparisons with classical state-of-the-art methods. Finally, potential directions for future improvements are outlined in the conclusion. © 2025 IEEE.

Cost-Optimal Building Energy System Scheduling Integrating Solar Irradiance Forecasting via LSTM-Attention-TCN Model
(2026) CAAI Transactions on Intelligence Technology, Cited 1 times.
DOI: 10.1049/cit2.70128
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105034804626?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: School of Electronic and Information Engineering, Suzhou University of Science and Technology, Suzhou, China; Department of Systems Engineering and Engineering Management, City University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong; Beijing Satellite Navigation Center, Beijing, China; Department of Automation, University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, China; College of Information and Communication, National University of Defense Technology, Changsha, China; School of Computer Science (National Pilot Software Engineering School), Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Beijing, China; School of Architecture, Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology, Xi'an, China; Anhui Province Key Laboratory of Intelligent Building and Building Energy Saving, Anhui Jianzhu University, Hefei, China
ABSTRACT: Building energy systems integrating multiple energy sources can effectively reduce energy consumption and facilitate renewable energy integration. Integrating electrical energy storage (EES) into these systems helps accommodate the increasing share of renewables; however, the stochastic and intermittent nature of solar power still poses challenges to supply reliability. This study proposes a photovoltaic (PV)-oriented storage scheduling strategy, in which short-term PV generation forecasts are applied to guide the operation of a building power supply network consisting of photovoltaic panels, the grid, and energy storage systems. The forecasting approach employs a hybrid framework combining a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to capture temporal dependencies, an attention mechanism to emphasise critical time steps, and a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) to map the enhanced features to PV outputs. Experimental evaluation using historical datasets under multiple weather conditions and time periods shows that the proposed LSTM-Attention-TCN model achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 20.45 W/m2 and a Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) of 0.94, outperforming both standalone LSTM and TCN models as well as their hybrid variants in terms of accuracy and robustness. By providing high-accuracy solar irradiance forecasts to guide energy storage operation and grid interaction, the proposed model enables more efficient and economical scheduling of building energy systems. Compared with an uncontrolled scenario, the LSTM-Attention-TCN-based scheduling reduces the total operating cost by approximately 52.1%, and achieves an additional 16.5% reduction compared to a conventional strategy without predictive coordination. In addition, compared to other hybrid forecasting models such as LSTM-TCN and TCN-Attention, the proposed model achieves the lowest total cost of CNY 14.83 and demonstrates superior scheduling efficiency, thereby enhancing the stability and flexibility of building energy utilization. © 2026 The Author(s). An Evaluation of Meteorological Variables Impact on Photovoltaic Power Generation Estimation Based on Deep Learning Model
(2025) Proceedings of 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology, ICCIT 2025, pp. 638 - 642, Cited 2 times.
DOI: 10.1109/ICCIT63348.2025.10989356
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105007517756?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: School of Civil Engineering, University of Granada, Granada, Spain; University of Granada, Department of Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence, Granada, Spain; University of Jeddah, Department of Computer and Network Engineering, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia
ABSTRACT: Accurate forecasting of photovoltaic (PV) power generation is essential for efficient grid integration and operation of solar energy systems. This study assesses a PV station in Scotland, UK, by analyzing the correlation between meteorological variables and power output. Two methods are employed: Pearson Correlation Coefficient and deep learning forecasting using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. The study uses four datasets, each incorporating a different meteorological variable alongside historical PV power data. Evaluation metrics include Mean Squared Error (MSE), Normalized Root Mean Squared Error (NRMSE), R-squared (R2), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). The analysis reveals that global total irradiance has the strongest positive correlation (0.92) with PV output, followed by temperature (0.66). Wind speed and relative humidity show negative correlations (-0.35 and -0.74, respectively). The LSTM model, trained with a 10-day input window, demonstrates the highest coefficient of determination with temperature range variable (99.48%) and the lowest NRMSE (1.77%). These findings highlight the significance of meteorological factors in optimizing PV power generation in Scotland. © 2025 IEEE.

AFFILIATIONS: NIT, Department of Electrical Engineering, Raipur, India
ABSTRACT: The deployment of a distributed generator (DG) and Volt-VAr control (VVC) devices in distribution systems offer energy management and voltage regulation. VVC devices include optimal coordination among on-load tap changers (OLTC), capacitor banks (CBs), and voltage regulators (VRs). The proposed method presents a two-stage energy management model (EMM) for the distribution system. In the first stage, a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) based machine learning technique (ML) is applied to predict solar irradiance accurately. In contrast, the second stage includes optimal coordination among DG and VVC devices to minimize substation energy demand while meeting system operational constraints. The proposed method is verified on the modified IEEE 69-node system. The performance of the MLP technique is compared with the seasonal auto-regressive integrated moving average (SARIMA) time-series model. The obtained results show the superior performance of MLP over SARIMA. In addition, the outcome of the simulated results reveals that the combined method of DG and VVC devices produces significant energy savings and mitigates voltage problems.  © 2024 IEEE.

ABSTRACT: Accurate long-term forecasting of Global Horizontal Irradiance (GHI) is essential for resilient solar energy planning in the face of climate uncertainty. This study presents a robust hybrid framework that integrates the Informer and Prophet models, supported by data preprocessing and feature selection using temperature, humidity, and the clear sky index. Prophet is used to analyze long-term trends and seasonality, while Informer effectively models complex temporal dependencies for extended forecasts. To account for uncertainty and improve the reliability of the forecast, Monte Carlo simulations generate probabilistic predictions with 95% confidence intervals over 30 years, based on historical data from 2004 to 2024. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of Informer in producing climate-resilient solar irradiance forecasts, contributing to the design of sustainable and adaptive energy systems.  © 2025 IEEE.

Advancements in AI-Based MPPT Algorithms for Optimizing Solar Power Systems in Electric Vehicle Charging Stations
(2025) 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Recent Trends in Computing and Smart Mobility, RCSM 2025, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1109/RCSM67767.2025.11507802
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105041471045?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: RKDF University, Department of Electrical Engineering, Bhopal, Gandhi Nagar, India
ABSTRACT: The rapid expansion in the infrastructure for electric vehicle (EV) charging together with the increase in integration with renewable energy sources is magnifying the requirements for highly efficient photovoltaic (PV) systems. For ensuring an optimal power point of the PV array under changing environmental conditions, an efficient tracking technique called Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) is required. This literature review offers a detailed exploration of the breadth of both conventional methods and advanced AI-assisted methods for MPPT, along with their evolution, capabilities, and limitations. Conventional methods, for example, P&O and INC, are widely used due to their simplicity but cannot track well under partially shaded situations amid fast solar irradiance fluctuations and nonlinear PV characteristics. AI-based techniques like artificial neural networks, deep learning architectures, and nature-inspired optimization algorithms bring an appreciable improvement in terms of tracking accuracy, adaptability, and avoided oscillations. These improvements will go a long way in improving the energy captured in the next generation of solar-powered EV charging systems and in making microgrids smarter. The paper has aimed to provide a compiled account of new advancements to realize the difference in performance trends and identify the significant research gaps lying in complex computations, real-time implementations, and scalability. From the present status of the field of research, this consolidated review provides a basis for furthering the development of more intelligent, hybrid, and highly efficient MPPT solutions for the growing number of modern PV applications. © 2025 IEEE.

Liu W., Han Y., Zhou X., Li J.
AUTHOR FULL NAMES: Liu, Weijia (56482434800); Han, Yongxiang (14421017500); Zhou, Xin (57221562804); Li, Jiaxin (57203891443)
56482434800; 14421017500; 57221562804; 57203891443
Dominant factors and uncertainties of surface shortwave cloud radiative forcing under different cloud types based on measurements at the central facility of the Southern Great Plains,USA [不同云种类地表云短波辐射效应的主控因子及其不确定性研究-以美国南部大平原地区中心观测站为例]
(2025) Transactions of Atmospheric Sciences, 48 (5), pp. 736 - 751, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.13878/j.cnki.dqkxxb.20241014001
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105021255227?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Hangzhou Meteorological Bureau, Hangzhou, 350001, China; Key Laboratory of Meteorological Disaster, Ministry of Education (KLME), Collaborative Innovation Center on Forecast and Evaluation of Meteorological Disaster (CIC-FEMD), Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology, Nanjing, 210044, China; Cornell University, Ithaca, 14850, NY, United States
ABSTRACT: Clouds play a crucial role in modulating the earth-atmosphere energy budget through their radiative cooling and heating effects.They are among the most significant yet uncertain components in climate projections due to their diverse types and complex cloud-radiation interactions.The surface shortwave cloud radiative effect (FCRE),defined as the difference between all-sky and clear-sky surface shortwave radiation,serves as a key indicator of the cloud-induced cooling effect.However,FCRE exhibits considerable variability and uncertainty across cloud types,attributable to large differences in macrophysical,microphysical,and optical cloud properties.Moreover,the dominant factors controlling these effects remain insufficiently understood for different cloud types.This study analyzes the FCRE characteristics and their driving factors for eight distinct cloud types-shallow cumulus (Cu),stratus (St),altocumulus (Ac),altostratus (As),cirrostratus (Cs),cirrus (Ci),congestus (Co),and deep convective clouds (Dc)-using 14 years of 15-minute resolution cloud-type classification and concurrent surface shortwave radiation measurements from the central facility of the Southern Great Plains in the United States.A new metric,relative FCRE(FRCRE),is introduced to complement FCRE and to reduce angular dependence effects.Using the XGBoost (extreme gradient boosting) framework and SHAP (Shapley additive explanation) values,the study interprets the dominant factors and uncertainties associated with both FCRE and FRCRE across cloud types.Key findings include:1) While FCRE magnitudes exhibit statistically significant positive correlations with cloud fraction and albedo and a negative correlation with solar zenith angle across all cloud types,detailed analysis reveals complex,nonlinear relationships that vary by cloud type.2) At the 95% confidence level,FCRE amplitudes range from -350 to 206 W·m-2 for low cloud fraction/albedo clouds (Cu,Ac,and Ci),from -926 to 371 W·m-2 for intermediate types (St,Cs,As),and from -1 172 to 289 W·m-2 for high cloud fraction/albedo clouds (Co and Dc),indicating substantial inter-cloud-type variability.3) The proposed FRCRE metric-functionally similar to FCRE-has three dominant predictors:cloud fraction,cloud albedo,and direct irradiance.FRCRE minimizes the influence of solar zenith angle and reduces uncertainty by 2.6% to 66.0% (mean reduction of 10.7%) compared to FCRE,with the most notable improvement observed for convective cloud types.4) For high cloud fraction/albedo clouds (Co and Dc),cloud albedo is the dominant driver of FRCRE,whereas for low cloud fraction/albedo clouds (Cu,Ac,and Ci),cloud fraction is more influential.These results highlight both the similarities and differences between FCRE and FRCRE,demonstrate the value of FRCRE in reducing uncertainty in estimating cloud radiative effects,and offer a refined understanding of cloud-radiation interactions.This study provides important insights for improving the representation of cloud-radiative processes in climate models. © 2025 Editorial Department of Transactions of Atmospheric Sciences. All rights reserved.

AUTHOR FULL NAMES: Wang, Xuecheng (57208927935); Xie, Peiran (59513357900); Xie, Yiyi (59513350700); Jiang, Hou (57190742653)

Localized solar radiation zoning by combining spatially continuous estimates and Gaussian mixture models
(2025) Journal of Atmospheric and Solar-Terrestrial Physics, 268, art. no. 106432, Cited 5 times.
DOI: 10.1016/j.jastp.2025.106432
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85214956002?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: School of Geography and Planning, Nanning Normal University, Nanning, 530001, China; Tianjin Puxun Power Information Technology Limited Company, Tianjin, 430010, China; State Key Laboratory of Resources and Environmental Information System, Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, 100101, China
ABSTRACT: With the increasing role of solar energy in the global decarbonization, precise geographical zoning of solar radiation becomes crucial. Traditional methods of solar radiation zoning struggle to accurately distinguish subtle spatial and temporal differences in solar radiation due to both sparse ground-based observations and the requirement for a predefined zone number, which limits their applicability for the demands of distributed photovoltaic system. This study introduces a novel method for localized solar radiation zoning, integrating spatially continuous solar radiation data with a Gaussian mixture model. High-precision spatiotemporal estimates of solar radiation are achieved by employing deep learning algorithms to analyze meteorological satellite imagery and digital elevation model data. The use of an infinite Gaussian mixture model along with variational inference allows for the adaptive determination of the number of solar radiation zones. The case study in Guangxi Province shows that incorporating Digital Elevation Model data reduces the root mean square error of global solar radiation estimates from 134.06 W/m2 to 87.68 W/m2 and accurately reveals temporal and spatial variability in both global and diffuse solar radiation. This approach not only prevents overfitting when the predefined upper bound surpasses the actual number of zones but also facilitates the development of zoning schemes that can range from fine-grained, capturing subtle variations, to coarse-grained, focusing on overall patterns. The outcomes lay a solid foundation for localized regional assessment and efficient utilization of solar energy resources. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd

Bayesian optimisation algorithm based optimised deep bidirectional long short term memory for global horizontal irradiance prediction in long-term horizon
(2025) Frontiers in Energy Research, 13, art. no. 1499751, Cited 7 times.
DOI: 10.3389/fenrg.2025.1499751
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/86000290650?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Department of Business Development and Technology, Aarhus School of Business and Social Sciences (BSS), Aarhus University, Herning, Denmark
ABSTRACT: With the continued development and progress of industrialisation, modernisation, and smart cities, global energy demand continues to increase. Photovoltaic systems are used to control CO2 emissions and manage global energy demand. Photovoltaic (PV) system public utility, effective planning, control, and operation compels accurate Global Horizontal Irradiance (GHI) prediction. This paper is ardent about designing a novel hybrid GHI prediction method: Bayesian Optimisation algorithm-based Optimized Deep Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory (BOA-D-BiLSTM). This work attempts to fine-tune the Deep Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory hyperparameters employing Bayesian optimisation. Globally ranked fifth in solar photovoltaic deployment, the INDIA Two Region Solar Irradiance Dataset from the NOAA-National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration was used to assess the proposed BOA-D-BiLSTM approach for the long-term prediction horizon. The superior prediction performance of the proposed BOA-D-BiLSTM is highlighted with the help of experimental results and comparative analysis with grid search and random search. Furthermore, the forecasting effectiveness is compared with other models, namely, the Persistence Model, ARIMA, BPN, RNN, SVR, Boosted Tree, LSTM, and BiLSTM. Compared to other forecasting models according to the resulting evaluation error metrics, the suggested BOA-D-BiLSTM model has minor evaluation error metrics, namely, Root Mean Squared Error: 0.0026 and 0.0030, Mean Absolute Error:0.0016 and 0.0018, Mean-Squared Error: 6.6852 × 10−06 and 8.8628 × 10−06 and R-squared: 0.9994 and 0.9988 on both dataset 1 and 2 respectively. The proposed BOA-D-BiLSTM model outperforms other baseline models. Thus, the proposed BOA-D-BiLSTM is a viable and novel potential forecasting model for effective distributed generation planning and control. Copyright © 2025 Madhiarasan.

Short-Term Irradiance Prediction Based on Transformer with Inverted Functional Area Structure
(2024) Mathematics, 12 (20), art. no. 3213, Cited 4 times.
DOI: 10.3390/math12203213
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85207666360?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: College of Mechatronics and Control Engineering, Shenzhen University, Shenzhen, 518054, China
ABSTRACT: Solar irradiance prediction is a crucial component in the application of photovoltaic power generation, playing a vital role in optimizing energy production, managing energy storage, and maintaining grid stability. This paper proposes an irradiance prediction method based on a functionally structured inverted transformer network, which maintains the channel independence of each feature in the model input and extracts the correlations between different features through an Attention mechanism, enabling the model to effectively capture the relevant information between various features. After the channel mixing of different features is completed through the Attention mechanism, a linear network is used to predict the irradiance sequence. A data processing method tailored to the prediction model used in this paper is designed, which employs a comprehensive data preprocessing approach combining mutual information, multiple imputation, and median filtering to optimize the raw dataset, enhancing the overall stability and accuracy of the prediction project. Additionally, a Dingo optimization algorithm suitable for the self-tuning of deep learning model hyperparameters is designed, improving the model’s generalization capability and reducing deployment costs. The artificial intelligence (AI) model proposed in this paper demonstrates superior prediction performance compared to existing common prediction models in irradiance data forecasting and can facilitate further applications of photovoltaic power generation in power systems. © 2024 by the authors.

Quantile calibrated ensemble deep learning framework for daily global horizontal irradiance forecasting
(2026) Energy Sources, Part A: Recovery, Utilization and Environmental Effects, 48 (1), art. no. 2651351, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1080/15567036.2026.2651351
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105034628634?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Department of Electrical Engineering, Rajkiya Engineering College, AKTU, Ambedkar Nagar, India; Department of Computer Application, Integral University, UP, Lucknow, India; Department of Information Technology, BBAU, UP, Lucknow, India
ABSTRACT: This study presents a chronology-preserving framework for daily global horizontal irradiance (GHI) forecasting over central India (21.78°N–27.23°N, 73.96°E–83.07°E) using national aeronautics and space administration (NASA) prediction of worldwide energy resource (POWER) reanalysis for 2020–2025. The pipeline uses a combination of targeted feature engineering, such as lagged persistence, multiwindow rolling statistics, sinusoidal seasonality encodings and clear-sky residuals, with heterogeneous base learners, such as Random Forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM) and short-term memory (LSTM). These models are aggregated by simple averaging, validation-weighted linear blending and a stacking ensemble whose meta-learner is a ridge regularized linear model trained on out-of-fold predictions to avoid information leakage. Probabilistic forecasts are computed with the help of quantile regression and are calibrated by conformal prediction to compute statistically valid prediction intervals. The proposed model gives the best results, with mean absolute error (MAE) = 0.085 W m−2, root mean square error (RMSE) = 0.110 W m−2, and coefficient of determination (R²) = 0.94, outperforming the results of the best single learner RF as well as the persistence and climatology baselines (MAE = 0.115 and 0.124). Conformal calibration enhances 90% prediction interval coverage probability (PICP) from 0.7713 to 0.8703, where interval sharpness is preserved as the mean prediction interval width (MPIW) ≈ 0.8790. Residual and binned-error diagnostics demonstrate that the stacking ensemble provides tighter and more symmetric residuals, lower variance and stable performance in monsoon and winter regimes, making it a robust and operationally interpretable model for grid-aware solar forecasting. © 2026 The Author(s). Published with license by Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.

Prediction and validation of solar power generation for solar electric vehicles using shading statistics on urban roads
(2025) Renewable Energy, 248, art. no. 123057, Cited 3 times.
DOI: 10.1016/j.renene.2025.123057
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105002398102?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Department of Energy Resources Engineering, Pukyong National University, Busan, 48513, South Korea
ABSTRACT: This study aims to analyze shading patterns on urban road segments using Google Street View panoramic images and to predict solar energy generation during vehicle operation through Monte Carlo simulations. Urban roads were divided into regular intervals, and Google Street View panoramic images were collected at each point. The study area was Nam-gu, Busan, where 3504 panoramic images were collected at 50-m intervals. These images were converted into hemispherical images. A deep learning model was applied to classify the sky and shading obstacles within these hemispherical images, and the annual solar trajectory was overlaid to calculate solar irradiance reduction rates by season and time of day. The road segments were categorized into seven types of shading patterns, and the hemispherical images were aggregated to analyze the statistical reductions in solar irradiance. Monte Carlo simulations were employed to derive multiple reduction rates for each shading type and predict the maximum, median, and minimum solar energy generation values. Additionally, three routes were subdivided into 10-m segments based on shading patterns, and solar energy generation estimates were made for each segment. Validation through real-world experiments demonstrated that the predicted energy generation closely matched the actual measurements across all routes. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd

Day-ahead Numerical Weather Prediction solar irradiance correction using a clustering method based on weather conditions
(2024) Applied Energy, 365, art. no. 123239, Cited 28 times.
DOI: 10.1016/j.apenergy.2024.123239
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85190818921?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Key Laboratory of Measurement and Control of Complex Systems of Engineering, Ministry of Education, School of Automation, Southeast University, Nanjing, 210096, China; Southeast University Shenzhen Research Institute, Shenzhen, 518063, China; Department of Electrical, Electronics and Computer Engineering, The University of Western Australia, Perth, Australia
ABSTRACT: Accurate solar irradiance forecasts can make solar power forecasts more reliable, which can help the power grid dispatch reasonably. In practice, Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) is widely applied in solar irradiance forecasts. In this paper, the statistical NWP Global Horizontal Irradiance (GHI) error analysis shows that the characteristics of NWP GHI error vary obviously under different weather conditions. However, existing correction methods are not designed contrapuntally for different weather conditions, resulting in poor correction performance. To solve this problem, a hybrid method is proposed to get day-ahead correction results for NWP GHI. Specifically, the hybrid method consists of three key parts, including Deep Clustering (DC), Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), and an Encoder–Decoder based Correction model (EDC). DC is used to categorize the historical samples into three clusters, the input of which is the multi-dimensional information series containing observed data and NWP data. After a feature selection by VMD, the correction models are trained on each cluster respectively. The performance of the proposed model is evaluated with a public dataset and an actual field dataset, and the results demonstrate that the accuracy has been effectively improved by the proposed method compared with other models. In addition, we find that adopting VMD is effective in improving the correction accuracy, and the root mean square error is reduced by 5.70% and 9.32% compared with models without it. © 2024 Elsevier Ltd

A Novel Framework for Solar Irradiance Prediction Integrating Signal Decomposition With Hybrid Time-Series Models
(2025) IEEE Access, 13, pp. 123414 - 123428, Cited 2 times.
DOI: 10.1109/ACCESS.2025.3580328
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105008666431?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: National Cheng Kung University, Department of Engineering Science, Tainan, 701, Taiwan
ABSTRACT: This study aims to improve the accuracy of solar irradiance forecasting by integrating signal decomposition techniques with deep learning and statistical models. Three decomposition methods—EMD, EEMD, and CEEMDAN—were combined with models such as LSTM, Bi-LSTM, GRU, Transformer, and statistical models such as ARIMA, ARCH, and GARCH were also implemented. Hybrid model architecture was developed to process high and low frequency signals separately in this research, respectively. Among all configurations, the EEMD–Transformer–GRU model achieved the best performance, with a MAPE of 7.87%, reducing prediction error by approximately 57% compared to non-decomposed models. These findings demonstrate that the integration of signal decomposition and hybrid deep learning significantly improves forecasting accuracy and offers a promising approach for renewable energy applications. © 2013 IEEE.

Hybrid TKNN-PCA-LSTM Model for Hourly Solar Irradiance Forecasting
(2025) 5th IEEE International Conference on Sustainable Energy and Future Electric Transportation, SeFeT 2025, Cited 1 times.
DOI: 10.1109/SEFET65155.2025.11255501
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105030324240?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: VNIT, Department of Electrical Engineering, Nagpur, India; NIT, Department of Electrical Engineering, Calicut, India
ABSTRACT: Accurate solar irradiance forecasting is essential for the efficient management and operation of electrical energy systems. This study presents a novel hybrid deep learning model that addresses the challenge of precise and reliable irradiance prediction. The proposed model integrates Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks with Temporal K-Nearest Neighbor (TKNN) and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for hourly solar irradiance forecasting. TKNN is employed for outlier detection and removal, PCA for dimensionality reduction, and LSTM for time-series prediction. The hybrid TKNN-PCA-LSTM model is evaluated across three geographically diverse locations in India. Its performance is benchmarked against both standalone and hybrid models using standard error metrics, including Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and the coefficient of determination (R2). The proposed model consistently outperforms the alternatives, achieving average RMSE and MAE values of 0.0847 and 0.0597, respectively. In addition, seasonal performance analysis is conducted, revealing the model's robustness and accuracy even during the highly variable and uncertain rainy season.  © 2025 IEEE.

Nishanth K., Saru Krishna S.
AUTHOR FULL NAMES: Nishanth, K. (58497723000); Saru Krishna, S. (58498302000)
58497723000; 58498302000
Enhancing Power Quality in Smart Grid-Connected Renewable Energy Systems Using A Hybrid Deep Learning-Based DSTATCOM: Self-Improved Jellyfish Optimizer (Si-Jo)
(2025) Optimal Control Applications and Methods, 46 (3), pp. 912 - 936, Cited 9 times.
DOI: 10.1002/oca.3238
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85212518300?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Research and Development, Mindscape Research, Tamil Nadu, Kuzhithurai, India
ABSTRACT: This manuscript introduces a robust stochastic optimization technique for real-time energy management in household solar (PV) storage systems, which addresses the constraints provided by the stochastic nature of solar power and load demand. Traditional offline solutions for day-ahead Battery Energy Storage (BES) scheduling frequently result in real-time energy losses, while online alternatives do not adequately reduce electricity prices. The proposed system combines an offline optimization model with a real-time rule-based controller and a deep learning-based Conditional Self-Attention Generative Adversarial Network (CSAGAN) for load and solar generation predictions to address these constraints. The War Strategy Optimization (WSO) Algorithm, which operates inside a receding horizon framework, optimizes BES dispatch set-points to lower daily electricity costs. The research also introduces a DSTATCOM-based hybrid technique for improving power quality (PQ) in grid-connected solar and wind systems, which makes use of a hybrid deep learning model consisting of Deep Belief Networks (DBNs) and Multilayer Perceptrons (MLPs). The Self-Increased Jellyfish Optimizer (SI-JO) generates control signals and optimizes the six-leg voltage source converter (VSC) and the buck-boost converter. MATLAB simulations show considerable increases in energy efficiency, harmonic distortion reduction, and system stability under various irradiance and grid fault scenarios, demonstrating the efficacy of the proposed techniques. © 2024 John Wiley & Sons Ltd.

Spatiotemporal Attention With Conditional Feature Modulation for Satellite-Based Solar Irradiance Prediction
(2026) IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters, 23, art. no. 1000605, Cited 0 times.
DOI: 10.1109/LGRS.2025.3647285
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105025650131?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: Jeonbuk National University, Department of Statistics, Jeonju-si, 54896, South Korea; Research Institute for Materials and Energy Sciences, Jeonbuk National University, Jeonju-si, 54896, South Korea; Jeonbuk National University, Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences, Research Institute for Materials and Energy Sciences, Jeollabuk-do, Jeonju-si, 54896, South Korea; Jeonbuk National University, Department of Statistics, Research Institute for Materials and Energy Sciences, Jeollabuk-do, Jeonju-si, 54896, South Korea
ABSTRACT: Accurate short-term solar irradiance forecasting is critical for grid stability, yet the existing deep learning models often struggle to capture complex dynamics over longer horizons. In this letter, we propose the attention-contextual U-Net (AC U-Net), a new architecture for multistep solar irradiance map prediction using GK-2A satellite imagery over the Korean Peninsula. The proposed model enhances a standard U-Net by integrating spatiotemporal attention and a featurewise linear modulation (FiLM) layer. This layer injects high-level contextual information directly into the model's bottleneck, allowing for dynamic feature adaptation. Experiments demonstrate that AC U-Net outperforms not only the persistence baseline but also deep learning-based competitors, such as ConvLSTM and HRNet. Our work demonstrates that conditioning on contextual features is a powerful strategy for improving long-range forecasting accuracy. © 2004-2012 IEEE.

Enhancing photovoltaic power generation nowcasting with sky image analysis using multi-modal attention networks
(2026) Solar Energy, 303, art. no. 114117, Cited 3 times.
DOI: 10.1016/j.solener.2025.114117
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105021088066?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: School of Information and Software Engineering, University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, Sichuan, Chengdu, 610054, China; School of International Education, Oxford Brookes College of Chengdu University of Technology, Sichuan, 610059, China; College of Nuclear Technology and Automation Engineering, Chengdu University of Technology, Sichuan, 610059, China; Department of OPT, School of Health Technology, Federal University of Technology, Imo State, Owerri, Nigeria; Division of Energy, Environment and Society, University of Dundee, Scotland, United Kingdom
ABSTRACT: The growing demand for renewable energy has heightened the importance of accurate photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting, especially under fluctuating weather conditions. Traditional and many deep learning-based models struggle to interpret the complex visual patterns in sky images, resulting in reduced prediction accuracy, particularly during periods of cloudiness or seasonal variability. In this study, we introduce a novel deep learning model that enhances solar nowcasting by dynamically identifying and emphasising the most informative features across multiple visual dimensions. The model introduces a compact multi-scale CNN backbone specifically tailored to the spectral–spatial characteristics of sky images, ensuring efficient feature extraction under real-time constraints. A custom lightweight attention mechanism is embedded to enhance cloud–irradiance saliency detection, delivering transformer-like selectivity while retaining low parameter and computational cost. These features are coupled with a regularised deep regression head that integrates high-level interactions, forming a unified architecture that advances photovoltaic nowcasting by balancing accuracy, interpretability, and efficiency. The study used the novel Sky Images and Photovoltaic Power Generation Dataset provided by Stanford University to evaluate the proposed model using evaluation metrics such as RMSE, MSE, MAE, MAPE, and R2. The proposed model achieves an overall RMSE of 2.259 and R2 of 0.913, with particularly strong performance on sunny days (RMSE of 0.461, R2 of 0.996) and consistent results under cloudy conditions (RMSE of 3.158, R2 of 0.824). Seasonal analysis reveals that the model maintains robust accuracy across different climatic conditions, with channel attention excelling during high-irradiance summer and autumn days, and spatial attention effectively capturing complex cloud structures in winter and spring. These outcomes depict the model’s ability to deliver more reliable short-term power forecasts by leveraging deeper visual understanding, ultimately contributing to more efficient solar energy management. © 2025 International Solar Energy Society.

AUTHOR FULL NAMES: Chen, Xiaolu (58159176800); Huang, Chenghao (57222062150); Zhang, Yanru (56023484600); Wang, Hao (56166541300)

Privacy-Preserving Personalized Federated Learning for Distributed Photovoltaic Disaggregation Under Statistical Heterogeneity
(2025) IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement, 74, art. no. 2529411, Cited 4 times.
DOI: 10.1109/TIM.2025.3569908
https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/105005980218?origin=resultslist

AFFILIATIONS: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, School of Computer Science and Engineering, Chengdu, 611731, China; Department of Data Science and AI, The Faculty of IT, The Monash Energy Institute, Monash University, Melbourne, 3800, VIC, Australia; University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, Shenzhen Institute for Advanced Study, Shenzhen, 518000, China
ABSTRACT: The rapid expansion of distributed photovoltaic (PV) installations worldwide, many being behind-the-meter (BTM) systems, has significantly challenged energy management and grid operations, as unobservable PV generation further complicates the supply-demand balance. Therefore, estimating this generation from net load, known as PV disaggregation, is critical. Given privacy concerns and the need for large training datasets, federated learning (FL) becomes a promising approach, but statistical heterogeneity, arising from geographical and behavioral variations among prosumers, poses new challenges to PV disaggregation. To overcome these challenges, a privacy-preserving distributed PV disaggregation framework is proposed using personalized FL (PFL). The proposed method employs a two-level framework that combines local and global modeling. At the local level, a Transformer-based PV disaggregation model is designed to generate solar irradiance embeddings for representing local PV conditions. A novel adaptive local aggregation mechanism is adopted to mitigate the impact of statistical heterogeneity on the local model, extracting a portion of global information that benefits the local model. At the global level, a central server aggregates information uploaded from multiple data centers, preserving privacy while enabling cross-center knowledge sharing. Experiments on real-world data demonstrate the effectiveness of this proposed framework, showing improved accuracy and robustness compared to benchmark methods. © 1963-2012 IEEE.
